clue.text: Bargain that displays 50% reduction — sneaky stuff

parts.note: a bargain is a steal, something bought cheaply

indicators.note: the word that is cut by half, keeping only its first two letters

explanation.surface: A shop advertises half-price goods, hinting the deal is somehow underhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that displays 50% reduction' means THAT halved: TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is secretive, furtive behaviour, the stuff of sneaking around unseen.

clue.text: A sun, over, exploding, having suppressed power

definitions.text: A sun, over, exploding, having suppressed power

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold down the letter for power inside them
blowing apart, so the letters of A sun over are rearranged

explanation.surface: A star finished, blown apart, its energy contained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' shuffles ASUNOVER; 'having suppressed' holds P inside. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a star's catastrophic explosion, so a sun bursting apart describes one exactly.

clue.text: Addition to play missing one accepted quotation?

indicators.note: one letter is left out of the joined words

parts.note: an extra is an addition
an act is a part of a play, or to play a role
A, one, shared between the two words so it appears once

explanation.surface: A supplementary scene for a play, cut except for one accepted line.
explanation.walkthrough: EXTRA and ACT overlap on their shared A, so one A goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken from a longer work, like a quoted excerpt.

clue.text: Unknown group of candidates backed — that's stupid

indicators.note: reversed, so the combined letters are read from the end

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
a pool is a group of candidates to choose from

explanation.surface: Supporting an unknown set of job applicants is called foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses YPOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for crazy, silly or daft.

clue.text: Something from previous times, old volume, used in support of fashion

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the word for the support

parts.note: a hanger supports clothes

explanation.surface: An old book put to use propping up the fashion world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' puts OV inside HANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is a leftover from an earlier era, something surviving from the past.

clue.text: Proceed to stop after last of wild crashes — that's a bit of luck

indicators.note: the word for stop is placed after the letters before it

parts.note: to proceed is to go

indicators.note: takes the final letter of each of the words wild and crashes

parts.note: to stop is to end

explanation.surface: A driver goes on after a wild crash and somehow escapes, which counts as lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' applies to both 'wild' and 'crashes', giving D and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected stroke of good fortune, a lucky break arriving just when needed.

clue.text: Crowd round King and Queen to get knighthood

indicators.note: the crowd word goes round the letter for king

parts.note: the gate is the crowd attending a sports match
R is for Rex, Latin for king
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A crowd surrounds the royal couple as someone is knighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts R inside GATE. The gate is British usage for match attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of the Garter is England's senior order of chivalry, into which knights are admitted.

clue.text: Painter, perhaps, one speaking in the last month

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the year's final month
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: An artist giving a speech in December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' suggests an artist, but here it is a house painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator paints and papers rooms, so a painter is one example.

clue.text: Candidate's angry comments following fellow heading off

indicators.note: the angry comments come after the shortened fellow
the first letter of the word for fellow is removed

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: An election candidate's furious remarks after a colleague leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops G from GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone entering a competition or contest, a candidate.

clue.text: Daughter felt unsettled in Dutch city

indicators.note: disturbed, so the letters of felt are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter uneasy while living in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is a city in South Holland, famous for its blue-and-white pottery.

clue.text: Subject having to swallow riposte

parts.note: to subject someone to something is to put them through it
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: Someone forced to swallow a sharp comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-down is a cutting remark or retort that humiliates someone.

clue.text: Concert not now recalled, involving contralto and I

indicators.note: the reversed word wraps around the next letters
called back, so the word for not now is read backwards

parts.note: not now means later

explanation.surface: A concert postponed and rearranged, featuring a contralto and the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns LATER into RETAL; 'involving' puts C and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, typically by a soloist or small group.

clue.text: Off-the-peg article brought in cash — a pile?

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the word for a pile

parts.note: a tower is a tall pile
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item sold brought in a heap of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts A inside TOWER to make TOWEAR. The ready is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-to-wear clothing is mass-produced in standard sizes, sold straight from the rack.

clue.text: Hideaway flushed out by intense skill

indicators.note: the hideaway word is driven out of the word for intense

parts.note: ardent means passionate, intense
a den is a hideaway or lair

explanation.surface: A hidden refuge exposed by a powerful skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flushed out by' removes DEN from ARDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Art is a craft or acquired ability, as in the art of conversation.

clue.text: Excited but doomed to see book forgotten, no longer popular

indicators.note: stirred up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
left out, so the letter for book is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled yet fated to watch their book sink into obscurity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgotten' removes B from BUTDOOMED; 'Excited' shuffles UTDOOMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Outmoded means old-fashioned, passed out of fashion and favour.

clue.text: Feeling nothing during extreme eclipse

indicators.note: the numb word sits inside the word for extreme

parts.note: outer means furthest out, extreme
numb means without sensation

explanation.surface: Numbness felt during a total solar eclipse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eclipse' is a verb, meaning surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to surpass it, as greater numbers surpass a smaller force.

clue.text: Version of it's missing from figure still

indicators.note: those letters are taken out of the word for figure

parts.note: a statistic is a figure, a number
a rearranged form of it's gives the letters T, I, S

explanation.surface: A rendering of a grammatical form left out of a still image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Version of' rearranges IT'S into TIS; 'missing from' removes TIS from STATISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless, unmoving, as still as can be.

clue.text: Wildly love the car that's not a US make

indicators.note: uncontrolled, so the letters are rearranged
the letter a is removed from car

explanation.surface: Adoring a car that is foreign rather than American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not a' removes A from CAR, leaving CR; 'Wildly' shuffles LOVETHECR. The surface's 'not a US make' misleads: the car is American.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevrolet is an American car manufacturer, a General Motors brand.

clue.text: Quiet son banned from school, having denied Cross

indicators.note: refused, so the letter for cross is taken out

parts.note: an excluded pupil is barred from school
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A quiet son is expelled from school after denying he is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having denied' removes X from EXCLUDED. Exclusion is the British term for expulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Secluded means private and sheltered from others, a quiet hidden spot.

clue.text: Fury seeing a reader cut short

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for reader is cut off

parts.note: a lector is a reader, especially in church or a university

explanation.surface: Rage provoked by watching someone reading being interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the last letter of LECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecto is one of the three Furies, avenging goddesses of Greek mythology.

clue.text: 1,000 line up to participate in kinky sex, fresh from the factory

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the rearranged sex
twisted, so the letters of sex are rearranged
in a down clue, up reverses the letters

parts.note: K is a thousand
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A thousand people queue to join an orgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses KROW to WORK; 'kinky' shuffles SEX into EXS; 'to participate in' puts WORK inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex-works describes goods sold directly from the factory, before delivery.

clue.text: Like clothing with a bit of extension, suitable for growth

indicators.note: just the first letter of the word extension

parts.note: arable land is fit for growing crops

explanation.surface: Garments with a little let-out room, fitting for a child still growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' gives E from 'extension'. 'growth' looks like children growing, but means crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing is something that can be worn, so the adjective describes garments generally.

clue.text: Bishop's attire, possibly

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: signals that the letters of attire may be rearranged

explanation.surface: What a bishop might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles ATTIRE after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a square cap worn by Catholic clergy, including bishops.

clue.text: Church celebration near to fishing port

parts.note: Whit is Whitsun, the Christian festival of Pentecost
by means near

explanation.surface: A church festival held close to the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitby is a fishing town on the North Yorkshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitby is a North Yorkshire harbour town with a long fishing tradition.

clue.text: Exclamation that makes American mother go topsy-turvy?

definitions.text: Exclamation that makes American mother go topsy-turvy?

parts.words: Exclamation that makes American mother go topsy-turvy?
parts.note: turn the US word for mother, M-O-M, upside down and the letters become an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An outburst that throws an American mum into a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Turned upside down, M becomes W, so the American MOM inverted reads as the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection expressing amazement or admiration, a cry of astonishment.

clue.text: Promise to orbit large planet

indicators.note: the promise word circles round the letter for large

parts.note: giving your word is a promise

explanation.surface: A vow to circle a giant planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to orbit' puts L inside WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: The world is our planet, Earth.

clue.text: Furniture worker helps out, working beside back (though not that of sofa)

indicators.note: the second part sits next to the first
in operation, so the letters of helps out are rearranged
signals that a letter is removed from the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: refers to the back of sofa, its final letter

explanation.surface: A furniture worker helps out next to the back, but not the sofa's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' shuffles HELPS OUT into UPHOLSTE; the back of 'sofa' is A, which 'though not' removes from REAR, leaving RER.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholsterer pads, springs and covers chairs and sofas, a craftsman of soft furnishings.

clue.text: Section of spectators accepting good competitor

indicators.note: the tier word takes in the letter for good

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats in a stadium

explanation.surface: Part of a crowd welcoming a fine sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts G inside TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a fierce, determined competitor, as in a tiger on the field.

clue.text: Runs with live section showing snack meal

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to live is to be, as in we are
a bit is a section or piece

explanation.surface: A live broadcast segment featuring runs, presented as a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' is the verb to exist, giving ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a light savoury snack.

clue.text: Regarding figures, understand everything? Not quite

parts.note: dig it is slang for understand it

indicators.note: the word for everything falls one letter short at the end

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about grasping the whole picture regarding numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of ALL. DIG IT is old slang for grasping something.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital means relating to numerals or data expressed as digits.

clue.text: Pull down wrecked store over middle of day

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover up the central letter of the word day

parts.note: store wrecked, its letters shuffled to E, S, T, R, O

explanation.surface: A shop demolished and wrecked in the middle of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' turns STORE into ESTRO, which replaces the middle letter A of DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull down a building is to demolish it, to wreck it completely.

clue.text: Sleeping commissionaire overlooks one over entry to theatre

indicators.note: misses out, so a letter is dropped from the word for commissionaire

parts.note: a commissionaire is a uniformed doorman at a hotel or theatre
O, a single over in cricket scoring

indicators.note: the first letter of theatre

explanation.surface: A dozing theatre doorman fails to notice something at the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooks' drops one O from DOORMAN; 'entry to' gives T from 'theatre'. A commissionaire is a British uniformed door attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive, as if asleep, like a volcano at rest.
